title: Regional quant+batch sensitivity worksheet — throughput vs quality
summary: Working worksheet for evaluating how quantization modes and batching knobs change throughput, latency and quality across regions and GPU pools. Goal: produce a recommendable policy that meets p99 latency SLO (<=200ms for chat short-turns) while maximizing throughput and minimizing cost for mixed production traffic. This is intentionally informal: contains raw measurements, quick calcs, and open questions for infra/product review.
assumptions:
- Workload: 80% short-turn chat (<=256 tokens), 20% long-form generation (avg 1024 tokens).
- Targets: p99 latency SLO 200ms for short-turns; cost target <$6 per 1M tokens for hosted tier; dedicated pools target 30% headroom at expected Q2 peak.
- GPU fleet mix simulated: us-west1 (A100-40GB), us-east1 (H100-80GB), eu-west1 (A100-80GB), ap-southeast1 (L4-48GB).
- Model variants: base-v1 (7B) and large-v1 (34B) with KV cache behavior enabled for repeated prefixes.
- Quant modes compared: FP16 baseline, Dynamic INT8, Static INT8 (calibrated), INT4 (GPTQ-ish).
- Batching knobs: target batch sizes [4, 8, 16, 32]. Continuous batching latency window 10ms.
- Quality metric: proxy is QA accuracy delta on dev prompts and average log-likelihood change; we log relative quality drop in percent and flag any >1.5% drop as material.

per_region_notes:
us-west1 (A100-40): most stable across FP16 and INT8; INT4 pushes memory pressure on 40GB for large-v1, requires sharded KV to avoid OOM. us-east1 (H100-80): best candidate for INT4 experiments on large-v1; lower p99 under higher batch but tail jitter increases for mixed short/long. eu-west1 (A100-80): conservative default for EU customers (compliance + lower variance). ap-southeast1 (L4-48): good for small models (7B) and embeddings; INT8 gives best cost-performance for embed-heavy workloads.
Notes: regional network egress to other clusters increases effective latency for fallback routing; include cross-region penalty ~8-12ms for remote fallbacks.
analysis_notes:
1) INT8 (calibrated/static) yields ~1.7x throughput vs FP16 with sub-1% quality hit for base-v1 across sampled evals; this is high ROI for hosted pipeline.
2) INT4 can double or triple throughput but quality regressions are model-dependent (large-v1 shows ~2.0-3.5% drop on code/QA). Reserve INT4 for non-critical reranking/embedding-like workloads.
3) Bigger batch sizes increase tokens/s linearly up to GPU saturations; however p99 for short-turns jumps >2x at batch 32 for mixed traffic because small queries wait behind long-form requests. Continuous batching window and request prioritization needed to protect short-turns.
4) KV/prefix caching reduces effective token compute by 18-40% for chat flows with repeated prefixes — this amplifies the benefit of quantization since cached tokens don't consume compute but still affect latency ordering.
5) For Dedicated pools we need to reserve extra headroom: INT8 gains are attractive but autoscaler must be tuned to avoid oscillation when traffic has diurnal spikes mixed with large generations.

open_questions:
- Calibration pipeline: does static INT8 cal pipeline cover both code and QA eval sets? Who owns per-model calibration timelines?
- Autoscaler hysteresis: recommended cooldown with INT8 workloads? current default 120s is too short leading to oscillation in simulated diurnal load.
- Fallback policy: prefer regional FP16 fallback or remote INT8 fallback when local capacity is saturated? Impact on p99 and egress costs needs concrete numbers.
- Observability: add per-token quality drift metric (rolling 24h) to surface quantization regressions quickly.

notes_to_self: This is a messy working sheet. When moving to playbook: separate short-turn SLA experiments from bulk throughput experiments. Consider adding a small micro-benchmark that simulates 90/10 short/long split with KV cache burst patterns. Keep raw CSV tab for perf team to reproduce numbers.
final_recommendation:
Short-term: enable StatINT8 default for base-v1 in hosted API in us-east1 + us-west1 for chat workloads with an opt-out flag for sensitive customers; enforce batch<=16 for short-turn endpoints and prioritized scheduling.
Medium-term: pilot INT4 on H100-80 in us-east1 for non-critical workloads (reranking/embeds). Monitor quality drift and rollback if >1.5% degradation across evaluation set.
Long-term: invest in automated calibration + per-model quality gates in Optimize pipeline; tie autoscaler cooldown to observed batch-induced latency volatility.
conclusion: Quantization + batching offers large unit-cost wins but requires coordinated changes across routing, autoscaling, and observability. The recommended incremental rollout (StatINT8 first, guarded INT4 experiments later) balances ROI and product risk.
